artboards.name: home-page
artboards.role: Marketing landing / home page for Forno Rosso pizzeria: header, hero, delivery info banner, featured pizzas grid, brand story section, footer. Single desktop-width (1440px) composition; no alternate breakpoints or revision artboards are present on the canvas.

ink.usage: header, hero, footer, dark card panels, primary body text on light backgrounds is a tint of this via opacity

slate.usage: secondary/muted text (paragraphs, meta copy) on light backgrounds

brand-red.usage: logo badge, primary CTA button fill, price text, active nav link + underline, eyebrow labels

white.usage: text on dark/red surfaces, secondary button border/text, card backgrounds

font_families.display: Fraunces (serif, italic-bold for logomark, semibold/bold for headings)
font_families.body: Geist (sans, used for nav, body copy, labels, buttons)

open_questions.detail: The Figma canvas contains a single 1440px-wide artboard with no tablet/mobile variants, so there is no design reference for how the header nav, 4-column featured grid, story section, or footer columns should reflow at narrower widths.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Implement standard responsive collapse (stacking columns, hiding/condensing nav into a menu) using conventional breakpoints, without a Figma reference to validate against.

open_questions.topic: Long pizza names are visually truncated in the rendered PNG
open_questions.detail: The JSON text nodes for 6:77 ('Funghi Selvatici & Tartufo') and 6:101 ('Prosciutto Crudo e Rucola') hold the full names, but the rendered PNG shows them cut off with an ellipsis ('Funghi Selvatici &...', 'Prosciutto Crudo e...') at the 302px card width, while the price stays on the same line.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Apply single-line ellipsis truncation (CSS text-overflow) to the PizzaCard name column, matching the PNG rather than wrapping to a second line.

open_questions.topic: Hero badge icon layer is named 'fire-extinguisher' but renders as a flame glyph
open_questions.detail: Node 6:679 in the hero eyebrow badge ('Authentic Neapolitan Woodfired') is named 'fire-extinguisher' in the Figma layer tree, but the PNG shows a simple flame-style glyph consistent with the wood-fired theme, not a fire-extinguisher icon.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Source a flame/fire icon for this badge (matching the PNG), treating the layer name as an icon-library artifact rather than the intended semantic.

open_questions.topic: No empty, loading, or error states are drawn for the featured pizzas grid or cart
open_questions.detail: The design only shows the grid fully populated with 4 items and a cart badge with a fixed count of 3; no state is drawn for zero results, a loading fetch, or an empty cart.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Build FeaturedSection and CartButton to accept dynamic data, but without a designed empty/loading/error state to implement against for this landing page in isolation.
